For any fuzzed caller, a call to airDrop routed through a contract implementing Bank.supportsToken correctly (returning keccak256("Nu Token")) must succeed and credit 20 tokens; the mutant's altered string makes supportsToken always revert, so the call fails and the balance stays 0.

For any caller accepted by the airdrop (a Bank returning the matching token hash with zero prior balance), one successful airDrop credits exactly 20 tokens; the mutant credits 40, breaking the invariant for some (any first-call) input.

For every admissible call, the reentrancy lock is released when airDrop completes (c._locked() == false afterwards); the mutant never resets _locked, so after any successful airDrop c._locked() reads true.

For any caller with a valid supportsToken interface and zero token balance, airDrop must succeed and grant 20 tokens; the inverted hasNoBalance guard makes such a call revert for every admissible fresh caller, so the success flag differs.
